title: OSHA crane operation and work area control practice questions
description: Free OSHA crane operation and work area control practice questions on 29 CFR 1926.1417 and 1424. Every answer is explained and linked.

questions.topic: Manufacturer procedures and their availability
questions.question: Where the manufacturer procedures are unavailable, who must develop the procedures related to the capacity of the equipment under 1926.1417(b)(3)?

options.A: The operator assigned to the equipment
options.B: A competent person named by the controlling entity
options.C: A registered professional engineer familiar with the equipment, who must also sign them
options.D: The employer's safety manager, with the operator's signature

questions.explanation: "Procedures related to the capacity of the equipment must be developed and signed by a registered professional engineer familiar with the equipment." Procedures for the operational controls, by contrast, "must be developed by a qualified person."

questions.topic: Manufacturer procedures and their availability
questions.question: The rated capacities are available in the cab only in electronic form, and a failure makes them inaccessible. What does 1926.1417(c)(2) require of the operator?

options.A: Finish the current lift and report the failure in writing at the end of the shift
options.B: Continue operating if a signal person watches the load
options.C: Continue operating from memory of the load chart for the rest of the shift
options.D: Immediately cease operations or follow safe shut-down procedures until the rated capacities are available in electronic or other form

questions.explanation: "In the event of a failure which makes the rated capacities inaccessible, the operator must immediately cease operations or follow safe shut-down procedures until the rated capacities (in electronic or other form) are available."

questions.topic: Manufacturer procedures and their availability
questions.question: Which items does 1926.1417(c)(1) name among the procedures that must be readily available in the cab at all times for use by the operator?

options.A: Rated capacities (load charts), recommended operating speeds, special hazard warnings, instructions, and the operator's manual
options.B: The project schedule and the site safety plan
options.C: The operator's certification card and medical card
options.D: Only the operator's manual

questions.explanation: The procedures, "including rated capacities (load charts), recommended operating speeds, special hazard warnings, instructions, and operator's manual, must be readily available in the cab at all times for use by the operator."

questions.topic: Operator attention and leaving the controls
questions.question: 1926.1417(d) bars the operator from activities that divert attention while actually operating the equipment, giving cellular phones as an example. What use of a cellular phone does the paragraph set apart?

options.A: Calls from the employer's dispatcher
options.B: Use for signal communications
options.C: Calls made while the load is suspended but not moving
options.D: Hands-free calls of short length

questions.explanation: The operator must not engage in any activity that diverts attention, "such as the use of cellular phones (other than when used for signal communications)."

questions.topic: Operator attention and leaving the controls
questions.question: Under 1926.1417(e)(1), the operator may leave the controls while the load is suspended only where all of the listed conditions are met. Which of these is one of those conditions?

options.A: The load is to be held suspended for no longer than normal lifting operations
options.B: The operator stays within sight of the load while doing other duties
options.C: Barricades or caution lines, and notices, are erected to prevent all employees from entering the fall zone
options.D: A signal person takes over the controls

questions.explanation: One condition is that "Barricades or caution lines, and notices, are erected to prevent all employees from entering the fall zone." The others include that the operator "remains adjacent to the equipment and is not engaged in any other duties" and that the load is held "for a period of time exceeding normal lifting operations."

questions.topic: Operator attention and leaving the controls
questions.question: Under 1926.1417(e)(1)(iii), who must determine that it is safe for the operator to leave the controls with the load suspended, and implement measures to restrain the equipment's functions?

options.A: The competent person
options.B: The signal person
options.C: A registered professional engineer
options.D: The controlling entity

questions.explanation: "The competent person determines that it is safe to do so and implements measures necessary to restrain the boom hoist and telescoping, load, swing, and outrigger or stabilizer functions."

questions.topic: Operator attention and leaving the controls
questions.question: Under 1926.1417(e)(2), when does the rule on leaving the controls with a suspended load not apply to working gear such as slings, spreader bars, ladders and welding machines?

options.A: When it weighs less than 75 percent of the maximum rated capacity
options.B: When it is suspended over an entrance or exit that is closed
options.C: When the operator has placed a tag in the cab
options.D: When its weight is negligible relative to the lifting capacity of the equipment as positioned and it is suspended over an area other than an entrance or exit

questions.explanation: The provisions "do not apply to working gear ... where the weight of the working gear is negligible relative to the lifting capacity of the equipment as positioned, and the working gear is suspended over an area other than an entrance or exit."

questions.topic: Tag-out, start-up and repairs
questions.question: The employer has taken one function of the equipment out of service, but not the whole equipment. What does 1926.1417(f)(1) require?

options.A: Only a verbal warning to the operator at the start of the shift
options.B: A tag in a conspicuous position stating that the function is out of service and is not to be used
options.C: A lock on the main disconnect, with no tag
options.D: Only an entry in the inspection record

questions.explanation: "Where the employer has taken a function(s) out of service, a tag must be placed in a conspicuous position stating that the function is out of service and is not to be used."

questions.topic: Tag-out, start-up and repairs
questions.question: A do not operate sign is on the starting control. Other than removal of the sign by a person authorized to remove it, what allows the operator to start the equipment under 1926.1417(f)(2)(i)?

options.A: The sign has been on the control for more than one full shift
options.B: The operator has verified that no one is servicing, working on, or otherwise in a dangerous position on the machine, and that it has been repaired and is working properly
options.C: The supervisor tells the operator by radio that the lift is urgent
options.D: A signal person is posted at the front of the equipment

questions.explanation: The operator must not start the equipment "until the sign has been removed by a person authorized to remove it, or until the operator has verified that: (A) No one is servicing, working on, or otherwise in a dangerous position on the machine. (B) The equipment has been repaired and is working properly."

questions.topic: Tag-out, start-up and repairs
questions.question: Equipment adjustments or repairs are necessary. What does 1926.1417(j)(1) require of the operator?

options.A: To tell the signal person orally before the next lift
options.B: To note it at the next monthly inspection
options.C: To inform, in writing and promptly, the person the employer designated to receive such information and, where there are successive shifts, the next operator
options.D: To notify every employee on the site in person

questions.explanation: "The operator must, in writing, promptly inform the person designated by the employer to receive such information and, where there are successive shifts, to the next operator." The employer then notifies affected employees "at the beginning of each shift."

questions.topic: Weather, safety devices and wire rope
questions.question: Under 1926.1417(h), what event requires the competent person to determine whether it is necessary to implement manufacturer recommendations for securing the equipment?

options.A: A local storm warning has been issued
options.B: The end of each work shift
options.C: A function has been taken out of service
options.D: The equipment is traveling with a load

questions.explanation: "When a local storm warning has been issued, the competent person must determine whether it is necessary to implement manufacturer recommendations for securing the equipment."

questions.topic: Weather, safety devices and wire rope
questions.question: The competent person has determined that there is a slack rope condition requiring re-spooling. What must be verified before starting to lift under 1926.1417(m)?

options.A: That the rope has been replaced
options.B: That the load moment indicator has been recalibrated
options.C: That a registered professional engineer has approved the lift
options.D: That the rope is seated on the drum and in the sheaves as the slack is removed

questions.explanation: "It must be verified (before starting to lift) that the rope is seated on the drum and in the sheaves as the slack is removed."

questions.topic: Rated capacity, load weight, brakes and counterweight
questions.question: The operator uses the method in 1926.1417(o)(3)(ii), and the device shows the load exceeds 75 percent of the maximum rated capacity at the longest radius that will be used during the lift. What must the operator do?

options.A: Not proceed with the lift until verifying the weight of the load by the method in paragraph (o)(3)(i)
options.B: Proceed if a competent person supervises the lift
options.C: Proceed after testing the brakes
options.D: Proceed after reducing the swing speed

questions.explanation: If it exceeds 75 percent, "the operator must not proceed with the lift until he/she verifies the weight of the load in accordance with paragraph (o)(3)(i) of this section."

questions.topic: Rated capacity, load weight, brakes and counterweight
questions.question: Under 1926.1417(o)(3)(i), the load weight is determined from a source or calculation method recognized by the industry, or other equally reliable means. When must this information be provided to the operator prior to the lift?

options.A: Only for lifts over the front area of wheel-mounted equipment
options.B: Only when the equipment is traveling with the load
options.C: When requested by the operator
options.D: Only when a storm warning has been issued

questions.explanation: "In addition, when requested by the operator, this information must be provided to the operator prior to the lift."

questions.topic: Rated capacity, load weight, brakes and counterweight
questions.question: In duty cycle and repetitive lifts where each lift is 90% or more of the maximum line pull, to which lift does the brake test in 1926.1417(s) apply?

options.A: Every lift in the cycle
options.B: Only the last lift of the shift
options.C: None of them
options.D: The first lift, but not successive lifts

questions.explanation: "In duty cycle and repetitive lifts where each lift is 90% or more of the maximum line pull, this requirement applies to the first lift but not to successive lifts."

questions.topic: Moving the equipment and the load
questions.question: The manufacturer does not prohibit traveling with a load, and the equipment will travel with one. What must the employer ensure a competent person does under 1926.1417(u)(2)(i)?

options.A: Supervises the operation, determines if rated capacity must be reduced, and makes determinations on load position, boom location, ground support, travel route, overhead obstructions and speed of movement
options.B: Signs a written travel permit for the whole project
options.C: Walks in front of the equipment as its only signal person
options.D: Inspects the equipment monthly while it travels

questions.explanation: The employer must ensure that "A competent person supervises the operation, determines if it is necessary to reduce rated capacity, and makes determinations regarding load position, boom location, ground support, travel route, overhead obstructions, and speed of movement necessary to ensure safety."

questions.topic: Moving the equipment and the load
questions.question: Under 1926.1417(z), a locomotive crane must not be swung into a position where railway cars on an adjacent track could strike it until what has been done?

options.A: The railroad has been notified in writing 24 hours ahead
options.B: It is determined that cars are not being moved on the adjacent track and proper flag protection has been established
options.C: The boom has been lowered and the load landed
options.D: The crane's travel brakes have been set

questions.explanation: It must not be swung there "until it is determined that cars are not being moved on the adjacent track and that proper flag protection has been established."

questions.topic: Swing radius hazards and multiple equipment
questions.question: The operator knows that an employee went to a swing radius hazard location. Under 1926.1424(a)(3)(ii), until when must the operator not rotate the superstructure?

options.A: Until five minutes have passed
options.B: Until the operator sounds the horn
options.C: Until informed, in accordance with a pre-arranged system of communication, that the employee is in a safe position
options.D: Until the load has been landed

questions.explanation: "The operator must not rotate the superstructure until the operator is informed in accordance with a pre-arranged system of communication that the employee is in a safe position."

questions.topic: Swing radius hazards and multiple equipment
questions.question: Under 1926.1424(a)(2)(ii), when may the employer mark the swing radius hazard areas with a combination of warning signs and high visibility markings on the equipment instead of barriers?

options.A: Whenever the operator prefers markings
options.B: When the work will last less than one shift
options.C: When a signal person is assigned to the equipment
options.D: When the employer can demonstrate that it is neither feasible to erect barriers on the ground nor on the equipment

questions.explanation: "Exception: When the employer can demonstrate that it is neither feasible to erect such barriers on the ground nor on the equipment, the hazard areas must be clearly marked by a combination of warning signs ... and high visibility markings on the equipment." The employer must also "train each employee to understand what these markings signify."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1424, Work area control (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Swing radius hazards and multiple equipment
questions.question: Where any part of a crane/derrick is within the working radius of another crane/derrick, who must institute a system to coordinate operations under 1926.1424(b)?

options.A: Each crane operator, separately
options.B: The controlling entity; if there is none, the employer (if only one employer operates the equipment) or employers
options.C: The equipment manufacturer
options.D: The signal person for each crane

questions.explanation: "The controlling entity must institute a system to coordinate operations. If there is no controlling entity, the employer (if there is only one employer operating the multiple pieces of equipment), or employers, must institute such a system."
